questions.q: How does the psalmist describe God?
questions.a: God is a refuge and strength to them, and he greatly helps them in trouble.

questions.q: What do the psalmists say they will not do, even if the earth changes and the mountains shake into the sea?
What makes the city of God rejoice?
questions.a: The channels of a stream make the city of God rejoice.

questions.q: What will the city of God not do?
questions.a: The city of God will not be shaken.

questions.q: What happens to the earth when God utters his voice after the nations roar and kingdoms shake?
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh of armies and the God of Jacob?
questions.a: Yahweh of armies is with them, and the God of Jacob is a stronghold to them.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do to wars?
questions.a: He makes wars cease to the end of the earth. He shatters the bow and cuts the spear in pieces, and he burns the wagons with fire.

questions.q: What does God tell the people to do?
questions.a: Be still and know that he is God.

questions.q: What will happen to God among the nations?
questions.a: He will be exalted among the nations and on the earth.

questions.q: What is the God of Jacob to them?
questions.a: The God of Jacob is a stronghold to them.

commentary.text: Verses 1–5 This psalm encourages to hope and trust in God; in his power and providence, and his gracious presence with his church in the worst of times. We may apply it to spiritual enemies, and the encouragement we have that, through Christ, we shall be conquerors over them. He is a Help, a present Help, a Help found, one whom we have found to be so; a Help at hand, one that is always near; we cannot desire a better, nor shall we ever find the like in any creature. Let those be troubled at the troubling of the waters, who build their confidence on a floating foundation; but let not those be alarmed who are led to the Rock, and there find firm footing. Here is joy to the church, even in sorrowful times. The river alludes to the graces and consolations of the Holy Spirit, which flow through every part of the church, and through God's sacred ordinances, gladdening the heart of every believer. It is promised that the church shall not be moved. If God be in our hearts, by his word dwelling richly in us, we shall be established, we shall be helped; let us trust and not be afraid.

Come and see the effects of desolating judgments, and stand in awe of God. This shows the perfect security of the church, and is an assurance of lasting peace. Let us pray for the speedy approach of these glorious days, and in silent submission let us worship and trust in our almighty Sovereign. Let all believers triumph in this, that the Lord of hosts, the God of Jacob, has been, is, and will be with us; and will be our Refuge. Mark this, take the comfort, and say, If God be for us, who can be against us? With this, through life and in death, let us answer every fear.
